claims.text: Overall valence electron count is the primary control on superconductivity in high-entropy alloys.
Replacing Zr with U can leave the average valence electron count nearly unchanged.
U substitution enhances spin-orbit scattering relative to Zr substitution.
U substitution creates additional scattering centers or disorder relative to the Zr analogue.
The enhanced spin-orbit scattering and disorder caused by U produce additional Cooper-pair breaking.
Additional pair breaking reduces the superconducting order parameter.
The proposed U-induced pair breaking lowers Tc.
The proposed U-induced pair breaking lowers Hc2.
The uranium f electrons in this alloy are delocalized.
U f electrons interact with conduction electrons differently from Zr-derived electronic states.
[TaNb]0.31(TiUHf)0.69 is a body-centered-cubic high-entropy alloy.
The Zr analogue [TaNb]0.31(TiZrHf)0.69 has a body-centered-cubic structure.
The constituent elements are stochastically distributed on the simple crystalline lattice.
Random alloying on the bcc lattice establishes a uniform electronic background.
The U-containing alloy should have a lower Tc than the Zr-containing analogue.
The U-containing alloy should have a lower Hc2 than the Zr-containing analogue.
U in the alloy should not exhibit a large localized magnetic moment.
Previous reports establish higher Tc and Hc2 for the Zr analogue.
The higher Tc and Hc2 attributed to the Zr analogue arise from an unperturbed electronic environment.
Using identical synthesis procedures will ensure similar disorder levels and structural characteristics in the two alloys.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts no large localized U moment and assigns pair breaking to spin-orbit coupling and disorder, but the falsification rule gives negligible magnetic scattering as an example that would falsify the mechanism. Negligible magnetic scattering is compatible with the stated nonmagnetic pair-breaking mechanism rather than decisive against it.

The comparison is said to maintain similar disorder levels, while the structural mediator says U substitution itself increases disorder or scattering centers. The text does not distinguish structural/configurational disorder from electronic scattering strongly enough to resolve this tension.
